main_text.l: item vestris, Dn. ◡Achatio, & Dn. Christopho-ro; Dominis meis gratiosissimis disputationem de Tribus Elochim. Ad portum cum nondum venerim, anchoram nondum figendam arbitror. Vos mihi portus eritis, Illustres Domini. Qua enim fronte illustria vestra nomina ingratus praeteream? Dignus certe nau fragio sim, ni Numina tam salutaria humilime venerer: ni vestras quoque imagines in gratitudinis meae templo suspendam. Nun-quam tu mihi quidem, generosissime Dn. Friderice, visus: attamen non ignotus. Vivam tui virtutumque tuarum imaginem in Fratribus tuis vidi: a Generoso Dn. Abrahamo praedicari audiui: liberalitatem sensi, & spem hanc concepi, fore ut in filio partem aliquando intuear, & debitae venerationis documenta edam certiora. To, generosissime Dn. Fabiane, videre & alloqui non ita pridem Berolini contigit humanitatem Domui vestrae hære-ditariam vidi: animi in me propensissimi indicia collegi, paucis dicam: expectatione omnia maiora inveni. Itaque ex eo ipso die, de mei in Generositatem tuam animi observantia publicis consignanda literis caepi co-gitare.

page.notes: The mark before "Achatio" and "Abrahamo" is a short curved sign (breve-like) over the A, printed before the name; I have kept it as ◡ and am not certain of its exact form. Small slash-like marks stand at the right edge of the column beside "nau", "in" and "Nun-" on the same lines; they may be printed marks or show-through and are not transcribed as text. The last line "deor" is the continuation of "vi-deor" and is set flush right, so it is part of the paragraph and not a catchword. "Fabiane" has no visible printed hyphen at its line end and is written whole.
